 Nick Saban makes pick for Alabama-LSU, identifies biggest concern for Tide
 Nick Saban made his pick for Alabama against LSU for Saturday's game in Baton Rouge.
 Mike Rodak 1 Former Alabama coach Nick Saban picked the Tide to win Saturday's game against LSU in Baton Rouge.
 "This is one of the most unusual home deals that you've ever seen," Saban said on ESPN's College Gameday. "LSU beats Alabama more when Alabama is at home, Alabama beats LSU more when they're playing at LSU -- which is a tough place to play. I think Bama gets it right. I'm all in for Alabama on this one."
 Alabama is a six-point favorite on major sports books, matching the 2021 SEC championship game against Georgia as the largest underdog spread for Alabama against any SEC team since it was a 9.5-point underdog to Florida in the 2008 SEC championship game. It also is tied for the second-largest underdog spread for Alabama against any team over that span, behind only a 7.5-point spread against Indiana last season.
 This is the first time since 2007 that Alabama is an underdog against LSU. It is also the first time since Alabama faced then-unranked Florida State in 2007 that the Tide has been an underdog against a lower-ranked team in the regular season.
 College Gameday panelists Desmond Howard and Pat McAfee, and guest picker Jason Sudeikis, all picked LSU.
 Earlier in the show, Saban identified what concerned him the most in the game for Alabama.
 "I think the thing I am most concerned about is how does Alabama's defense play against LSU's offense?" he said. "I don't care how they do it. You can talk about stealing signals, you can talk about how you disguise your defense. But when LSU and Lane Kiffin know what you're in, they are going to dial up the No. 1 best play that they can run against that look and you're always going to be behind on defense -- you're always going to be one play behind. They take advantage of that as well as anybody in college football.
 "How LSU's defense can not let them steal their signals and disguise what they're in pre-snap so they have to figure out after the ball turns over."
 Alabama will get back starting wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, starting center Racin Delgatty and starting defensive tackle Terrance Green for the game, while the status of cornerback Zabien Brown, running back EJ Crowell and guard William Sanders -- who all remained questionable on Friday night's availability report -- will be updated at 1 p.m. CT before the 2:30 p.m. CT kick in Tiger Stadium.
 "I think getting Ryan Coleman-Williams back is going to be helpful to them, too," Saban said earlier Saturday. "He was sort of the go-to guy. He can take the top off the defense, so that will be helpful."
